record.context_brief: whether every minimal relation comes from RF-matrices
record.original_question: Let Gamma = <g1, ..., ge> be a numerical semigroup and let p be a pseudo-Frobenius number of Gamma. An RF-matrix of p is an e x e matrix (a_ij) with a_ii = -1, a_ij in N for i != j, and sum_j a_ij g_j = p for every row i; subtracting two rows gives a relation in ker(phi), called an RF-relation. Are all minimal relations of a numerical semigroup RF-relations?

evidence.quote: Let p be a pseudo-Frobenius number of a semigroup Γ = hg1,...,gei. An RF-matrix (row-factorization matrix) of p is an e×e matrix (aij) ... and (a+,a−) is called an RF-relation of Γ . artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma = \langle g_1, \dots, g_e \rangle \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be a numerical semigroup, that is, a submonoid of $(\mathbb{N},+)$ minimally generated by positive integers $g_1, \dots, g_e$ with $\gcd(g_1,\dots,g_e)=1$. Let $\varphi: \mathbb{N}^e \to \Gamma$ be the surjection $\varphi(\alpha) = \sum_i \alpha_i g_i$, and consider the kernel congruence $\ker(\varphi) = \{(\alpha,\beta) \in \mathbb{N}^e \times \mathbb{N}^e : \varphi(\alpha) = \varphi(\beta)\}$. An element $p \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \Gamma$ is called a pseudo-Frobenius number of $\Gamma$ if $p + g_i \in \Gamma$ for all $i = 1,\dots,e$.

For a pseudo-Frobenius number $p$ of $\Gamma$, an RF-matrix (row-factorization matrix) of $p$ is an $e \times e$ integer matrix $A = (a_{ij})$ such that:
(i) $a_{ii} = -1$ for all $i$;
(ii) $a_{ij} \in \mathbb{N}$ for all $i \neq j$;
(iii) $\sum_{j=1}^e a_{ij} g_j = p$ for every row $i$.

Given two distinct rows $i,k$ of an RF-matrix, write the difference of these rows as $\alpha - \beta$ with $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{N}^e$ disjointly supported; the pair $(\alpha,\beta)$ then lies in $\ker(\varphi)$ and is called an RF-relation of $\Gamma$.

A minimal relation of $\Gamma$ is an element of a minimal generating set of the congruence $\ker(\varphi)$.

Question: Is it true that for every numerical semigroup $\Gamma$, every minimal relation of $\Gamma$ is an RF-relation arising from some RF-matrix of some pseudo-Frobenius number of $\Gamma$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question (originally posed by Herzog–Watanabe) appears to remain open in general. Recent works only verify the property in special cases — e.g., for symmetric numerical semigroups minimally generated by an almost arithmetic sequence with embedding dimension 4 or 5 — and the question continues to be cited as an open problem in survey/problem lists on numerical semigroups.
